result.title: Autonomous AI Agents Systematically Diverge From Human Preferences in Proof Formalization
result.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) systems have ushered in a new age of proof abundance, but helping humans understand these proofs requires new attention to the differences in how AI agents and humans pursue a proof-making task. We present "simulated collaboration", a methodology that allows us to examine two key questions: (1) the relative attention AI agents pay to surface syntax or, conversely, deeper underlying semantics, and (2) how and where AI agent preferences for what to do next diverge from human preferences. On a set of nine major human collaborations in Lean with 4.7M definitions across more than 6K commits, we find that, over the course of proof construction, AI agents (1) are far more strongly drawn than humans to explicitly marked gaps; (2) show a relative aversion to densely connected proof centers and to complex or surprising proof goals; and (3) are relatively attracted to surprising proof bodies, which they tend to regularize toward baseline. Our results highlight important blind spots and potential interventions for future human-AI collaboration in mathematics.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出「simulated collaboration」方法，在九个 Lean 形式化协作项目（逾 6K 次提交）中对比 AI agent 与人类的证明构建行为，发现 agent 更被显式标记的缺口吸引、相对回避稠密连接的核心与复杂目标，并对「惊人」证明体趋向正则化。
AI.relevance_reason: 其关于表层语法与深层语义注意力、以及下一步行动偏好偏差的刻画，可能为诊断 latent 推理状态是否保留任务必要语义、评估 LOOK/STOP 类证据筛选与停止决策的系统性偏差提供可核查的类比框架，但领域与方法相距较远，需较多核查。
